newsitem.title: USA: Short covering drives NYMEX natgas to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Short covering drives NYMEX natgas to higher close.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, with short covering in the face of a steady cash and warmer weather forecasts next week still driving the complex.
August climbed 4.8 cents to close at $2.116 per million British thermal units. September settled 4.4 cents higher at $2.126. Other deferreds ended up by 1.3 to 3.7 cents.

"I think the Merc boys decided the cash wasn't coming off and rushed to cover today. They were tripping over each other to get out," said one Houston trader, adding forecasts for warmer East Coast weather next week helped prompt some buying.
Despite fairly mild East Coast and Midwest weather this week, traders noted physical prices have been steady to firm, raising the possibility of higher values next week if the heat returns.
In addition, they said Monday's seven cent cash to futures premium and a 30 cent spread to winter also had shorts nervous.

Technical traders said short covering kicked in early today when downside momentum stalled just below key support at $2.055. They now pegged support in August at today's low of $2.051, with psychological support at $2. Resistance was seen at $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.25-2.26. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices held steady at about $2.10. Midcon pipes were unchanged to a penny higher in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas was quoted little changed in the high-$2.30s.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 70 to 100 bcf versus a 90 bcf build for the same week last year.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip gained 3.3 cents to $2.206. NYMEX said 39,109 contracts traded, up sharply from Monday's revised tally of 20,593.

On the KCBT, August finished five cents higher at $2.005, while deferreds ended up by three to five cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.2 cent to 11.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 72 lots traded, up from Monday's total of 26.
